title: two-branch house: living room with two lamps and a hallway with two two-way switches
style: Cooperative and tidy: describe the circuit in two or three messages, in full sentences.
facts: It is the wiring of your house. The current comes in through a battery (call it batt). A wire from the panel (panel_wire) leaves it and then goes through the main fuse (main_fuse); after that there is a wire you call after_main that feeds two branches. LIVING ROOM: from after_main, through the living room switch (living_sw, which closes the circuit when it is up), runs the wire living_wire, from which two lamps hang in parallel, lamp_a and lamp_b. HALLWAY: the hallway light (hall_light) is controlled from both ends by two two-way switches (hall_sw1 next to the panel and hall_sw2 next to the light), joined by two wires, wire_a and wire_b: hall_sw1 sends the current from after_main to wire_a when it is up and to wire_b when it is down; hall_sw2 picks up wire_a when it is up and wire_b when it is down and feeds hall_light. (That is, the hallway is lit when both two-way switches are in the same position.) STATE AT THE START: living_sw down, hall_sw1 up, hall_sw2 up, all lamps and the fuse in good condition. EVENTS, in this order: 1) you raise living_sw; 2) you lower hall_sw1; 3) lamp_a blows; 4) the main fuse (main_fuse) blows; 5) you repair it; 6) you lower hall_sw2.
questions: Which lamps are lit at the start (before any event)?
Why is hall_light not lit after lowering hall_sw1 (event 2)?
Why is lamp_b not lit when the main fuse (main_fuse) blows (event 4)?
Why did hall_light change over the course of all the events?
I would like to see the timeline of all the lamps.
EXTENSION: tell it that after all that (as event 7) you lower living_sw, and ask which lamps are lit now at the end.
